question: Ascent — ATK, 3v3, no spike, 0:53 left. Your entry teammate is running out into A Main ahead of you toward the choke into A. As trailing support, what is the highest-EV play?

options.label: Trade-hold: swing just behind your entry with your crosshair on the same angle, ready to re-peek and trade if he dies
options.explication_courte: The entry's job is to draw the first bullet; yours is to punish it. Staying one step behind on the same angle means if he trades down a defender you instantly re-peek the wounded/reloading enemy and swing the fight back to 3v2 or better.

sources_option.citation: Support players trade entries by holding a beat behind and re-peeking the same angle the moment the entry fight opens

options.label: Sprint out first past your entry to take the A Main duel yourself with more HP
options.explication_courte: Overtaking your own entry collapses two players into the same opening angle — if the defender holds the pixel, you both die to one hold and there is nobody left to trade. Order of entry is a structure, not a race.

sources_option.citation: The support follows the entry to trade — not ahead of them; the entry clears the angle first and the second player punishes the response

options.label: Hold back at spawn side and let the entry clear A Main solo before you commit
options.explication_courte: Playing safe keeps you alive, but a solo-entry with no trade behind it is a coinflip; if he dies for free you're a slow 2v3 with the clock burning. Passive support wastes the entry's sacrifice.

sources_option.citation: An entry with no trade support behind it turns a sacrifice into a free kill for the defense; commit close enough to trade

options.label: Peel off alone toward mid to look for a flank while your entry hits A
options.explication_courte: Splitting off in a 3v3 abandons your entry to a 1v-however-many on A and isolates you on a lurk with no info. You turn one grouped hit into two under-manned fights the defense wins in detail.

sources_option.citation: Splitting numbers on a low-man round lets the defense fight you piecemeal; stay grouped to keep the trade chain intact

explication_longue: In a 3v3 with your entry already committing to A Main, the round is decided by whether his first duel gets traded. That is the entire job of the trailing support: be close enough, on the same angle, that the instant the entry fires (and possibly dies) you re-peek and punish the defender who is now reloading, low, or repositioning off the kill. Swinging one beat behind on the same line keeps the fight a 1-for-1-at-worst instead of a free defensive pick. Overtaking your own entry is the classic support mistake — two bodies pour into one held angle, one defender's pre-aim kills both, and there is nobody left to trade. Holding all the way back keeps you alive but wastes the entry's sacrifice: a solo A Main hit with no trade is a coinflip that leaves you a slow 2v3 on the clock. Peeling to mid for a flank shreds your numbers in a round where you can't afford it — the defense simply fights your two halves one at a time. Elite support play is unglamorous: trail tight, mirror the angle, trade the entry.

sources.citation: The entry-and-trade pair is the core of a site take: entry draws the fight, support trades within a second on the same angle
